home.title: వడ్డన
home.lede: A diner scans the QR, orders in Telugu or English, and the kitchen gets the ticket. No app and no login at the table.
home.step1.title: Scan
home.step1.body: Each table has its own QR. The menu opens on the diner’s phone.
home.step2.title: Confirm
home.step2.body: Staff see the new order, confirm it or reject it with a reason.
home.step3.title: Cook and bill
home.step3.body: The kitchen marks it ready. The bill builds from the rounds, then cash or UPI.
home.faq.printer.q: Will Telugu print on a thermal printer?
home.faq.printer.a: Browser print works. Raw printer text usually has no Telugu glyphs, so a silent print has to send a picture of the ticket.
home.faq.upi.a: The diner can start a UPI payment or pay at the counter. Staff mark cash and UPI as paid. A payment gateway is not connected yet.
home.faq.telugu.a: You type Telugu and English side by side. Dish names are never translated by the app. A missing Telugu name falls back to English.
home.faq.offline.a: The menu stays on screen. Sending an order waits until the connection is back.
